# sysutils_file_line (Resource)

Manages a single `line`, or a `block` of lines between marker comments, inside an existing text file without taking over the rest of the file, like Ansible's `lineinfile` and `blockinfile`. Changes are written atomically and keep the file's mode and ownership. On destroy, only the managed line or block is removed.

Use it for files that other packages or tools also edit, such as `/etc/hosts`, `/etc/ssh/sshd_config` or `/etc/fstab`, where [`sysutils_file`](./file.md) would take over the whole file.

## Example Usage

### Single lines

```terraform
# Add a static host entry to /etc/hosts. Destroy removes only this line.
resource "sysutils_file_line" "db_host" {
  path = "/etc/hosts"
  line = "10.0.0.5 db.internal db"
}

# Replace the (possibly commented-out) PermitRootLogin setting in place, so
# that it stays in the global section. If no line matches, the line is added
# after the last line matching insert_after, or at the end of the file.
resource "sysutils_file_line" "sshd_root_login" {
  path         = "/etc/ssh/sshd_config"
  regexp       = "^#?PermitRootLogin\\s"
  line         = "PermitRootLogin no"
  insert_after = "^#?Port\\s"
}

# Reload sshd whenever the managed line changes.
resource "sysutils_exec" "reload_sshd" {
  command = ["systemctl", "reload", "ssh"]
  triggers = {
    line = sysutils_file_line.sshd_root_login.line
  }
}
```

### Blocks

```terraform
# Keep a block of cluster nodes in /etc/hosts, between marker comments:
#
#   # BEGIN cluster nodes
#   10.0.1.1 node1
#   ...
#   # END cluster nodes
locals {
  nodes = {
    node1 = "10.0.1.1"
    node2 = "10.0.1.2"
    node3 = "10.0.1.3"
  }
}

resource "sysutils_file_line" "cluster_hosts" {
  path   = "/etc/hosts"
  marker = "# {mark} cluster nodes"
  block  = join("", [for name, ip in local.nodes : "${ip} ${name}\n"])
}

# Create the file if it does not exist yet, and put the block at the top.
resource "sysutils_file_line" "profile_path" {
  path          = "/etc/profile.d/app.sh"
  create        = true
  insert_before = "BOF"
  block         = <<-EOT
    export APP_HOME=/opt/app
    export PATH="$APP_HOME/bin:$PATH"
  EOT
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `path` (String) Absolute path of the file to edit. Must be in canonical form (no `.`/`..` segments, duplicate or trailing slashes) and must not be `/`. A symlink at `path` is refused. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `block` (String) Lines to keep between a `BEGIN` and an `END` marker line (see `marker`). A single trailing newline, as produced by heredocs, is ignored. Exactly one of `line` and `block` must be set.
- `create` (Boolean) Create the file (mode `0644`, owned by the user running Terraform, missing parent directories with mode `0755`) if it does not exist. If `false`, a missing file is an error. Destroy never deletes the file. Defaults to `false`.
- `insert_after` (String) Where to insert the line or block if it is not present: `"EOF"` for the end of the file, or a Go regular expression to insert after the last matching line (at the end of the file if no line matches). Conflicts with `insert_before`. If neither is set, content is appended at the end of the file. Only affects where missing content is added; content that is already present is never moved.
- `insert_before` (String) Where to insert the line or block if it is not present: `"BOF"` for the beginning of the file, or a Go regular expression to insert before the last matching line (at the end of the file if no line matches). Conflicts with `insert_after`.
- `line` (String) The exact line (without line break) that must be present in the file. Exactly one of `line` and `block` must be set.
- `marker` (String) Only with `block`. Template for the marker lines around the block; `{mark}` is replaced with `BEGIN` and `END`. Use a distinct marker for every block in the same file. Defaults to `"# {mark} MANAGED BY TERRAFORM"`.
- `regexp` (String) Only with `line`. A [Go regular expression](https://pkg.go.dev/regexp/syntax) selecting an existing line to replace. If any line matches, the **last** matching line is replaced by `line`; otherwise `line` is inserted as if `regexp` were unset. `line` should itself match `regexp`, so that repeated applies converge.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Resource identifier: `path`, a colon, and then `marker` for blocks or `line` for lines.

## Behavior

### Lines

With only `line` set, the resource makes sure that an identical line exists somewhere in the file. If it does not, the line is inserted according to `insert_after` / `insert_before`, and at the end of the file by default.

With `regexp` set, the **last** line matching the regular expression is replaced by `line`. If no line matches, `line` is inserted as if `regexp` were unset. Choose a `line` that itself matches `regexp`, for example `regexp = "^#?Port\\s"` with `line = "Port 2222"`. Otherwise the replaced line no longer matches and the next apply may replace a different line.

Changing `line` replaces the previous line where it is instead of adding a second one.

### Blocks

With `block` set, the content is kept between two marker lines generated from `marker`, where `{mark}` becomes `BEGIN` and `END`:

```
# BEGIN MANAGED BY TERRAFORM
...block...
# END MANAGED BY TERRAFORM
```

Content between the markers is replaced in place when it differs. If the markers are not found, the whole block, including the markers, is inserted according to `insert_after` / `insert_before`. Use a distinct `marker` for every block in the same file. The markers must be comment lines in the file's syntax, so for files that don't use `#` comments, set `marker` accordingly (for example `"; {mark} MANAGED BY TERRAFORM"`).

### Writing the file

- Nothing is written if the file already has the desired content, so the modification time only changes when content does.
- Changes are written to a temporary file in the same directory, which gets the original file's owner, group and mode before it receives any data, and is then renamed over the original. Other processes see either the old or the new file, never a partial one.
- Right before the rename, the provider checks that the file was not changed or replaced since it was read, and fails without writing if it was. Several `sysutils_file_line` resources editing the same file are serialised by the provider, so they can be applied in parallel safely.
- The file must be a regular text file with `\n` line endings; `\r\n` files are not supported. Files larger than 64 MiB are refused.

## Drift Detection

On refresh, the provider reads the file and looks for the managed content:

- If the managed line or block is missing, or the file was deleted, the resource is removed from state and the next plan shows it being created again.
- If the content between the block markers, or the line selected by `regexp`, was changed, the actual content is recorded in state. The plan then shows an in-place update from the actual to the configured value.

Changes to `regexp`, `insert_after`, `insert_before` or `create` alone don't move content that is already present.

## Destroy

Destroy removes only the managed content: every line identical to `line`, or the first block between the markers. The rest of the file, including a file created because of `create = true`, is left in place. A line replaced via `regexp` is **not** restored to its original value. If the managed line already existed before Terraform managed it, destroy removes it anyway.

## Import

An existing line or block can be imported with an ID made of the file's path, a colon, and then the exact line, or the `marker` template for a block. IDs whose part after the colon contains `{mark}` are imported as blocks:

```shell
# A line: <path>:<line>
terraform import sysutils_file_line.db_host '/etc/hosts:10.0.0.5 db.internal db'

# A block: <path>:<marker>, recognised by the {mark} placeholder
terraform import sysutils_file_line.cluster_hosts '/etc/hosts:# {mark} cluster nodes'
```

The path ends at the first colon, so files whose path contains a colon cannot be imported. After import, `regexp`, `insert_after` and `insert_before` are unset in state. They only affect where missing content is inserted, so setting them in the configuration causes an in-place update that doesn't change the file.

## Caveats

- Consistent with the provider's [security model](../index.md#security-model), a symlink at `path` is refused, and so is anything else that is not a regular file. Symlinks in the parent components of `path` are followed. If the file is replaced by a symlink after creation, refresh fails and the symlink's target is never modified. On destroy, a symlink or other non-regular file at `path` is left untouched, with a warning.
- The rename gives the file a new inode, which breaks hard links and does not carry over extended attributes, ACLs or SELinux labels. If `path` is a mount point, as a bind-mounted `/etc/hosts` in a container is, the rename fails with `EBUSY`. In that case, and only then, the file is rewritten in place, which is not atomic.
- Preserving an owner other than the user running Terraform requires the privileges to `chown` the replacement file, normally root.
- The lock that serialises edits only covers this provider. Other tools editing the file at the same time are only detected by the check before the rename, and a `sysutils_file` managing the same file conflicts with this resource.
- The resource only works on Unix-like systems.
